rebelrebel

Fast interactive maps in R, drawn in the browser by MapLibre GL JS, with the sea in mind: tracks, stations, gridded values, areas and labels over the sea floor. In the company of leaflet, mapview and tmap, rebelrebel keeps the data in DuckDB: a parquet file of millions of rows reaches the page as vector tiles, so the map stays fast, and its colours, legend and choices change in the page without asking R again.

A map is built with the pipe, a layer at a time, in the words of ggplot2:

library(rebelrebel)

rr_map(rr_example("trawlsurvey"), title = "A survey") |>
  rr_path(group = vid, time = time, colour = behaviour) |>
  rr_point(colour = speed, popup = c(vid, time, speed), minzoom = 8, visible = FALSE)

Printed at the console, the map opens in the viewer, served from your machine. rr_bundle() writes it as a folder that opens from its index.html, with no R and no network but the base map’s.

What there is

  • Layers: rr_point(), rr_path() (rows joined in time, a line per group), rr_line(), rr_segment() (a line from each row’s start to its end), rr_polygon(), rr_text(); and rr_layer() for a layer in MapLibre’s own terms.
  • Data: a parquet file, folder or glob, a lazy DuckDB table, a data frame or an sf object. A bare name is a column, a string a value: colour = speed or colour = "#c0392b".
  • Colours from the data: Okabe-Ito for up to eight values, Paired for up to twelve, Glasbey’s 32 beyond; viridis for numbers, dates and ordered values; any palette by name, by colours or by value with palette.
  • The sea floor: base maps that show it (EMODnet’s, light and dark, Esri’s ocean), and depth, relief and contours from your own grid (rr_tiles_dem(), rr_tiles_mbtiles()).
  • In the page: popups, hover labels, a choice of colouring, choices of what to show, a time panel under the map (rr_time()), notes and verdicts written by readers, and the whole view in the page’s address.

Installation

The example data are Git LFS objects, so install from a clone that fetches them, with Git and Git LFS on the machine:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_git("https://github.com/einarhjorleifsson/rebelrebel", git = "external")

remotes::install_github() would install the LFS pointers instead of the data; rr_example() then stops and says so.

Status

Young, and changing: the layer functions are new, and a one-call rr_view(), cells (rr_grid()), depth (rr_relief(), rr_contour()) and figures saved at a chosen size and resolution (rr_save()) are to come. The package began as the map viewer of the R package ramb.
